faqs.question: What are some easy Halloween movie trivia questions?
faqs.answer: Try these: what is Jack Skellington's ghost dog called (Zero), what is the talking cat in Hocus Pocus called (Binx), and how old is Michael Myers in the 1963 opening of Halloween (six). Nine of this quiz's 53 questions are tagged easy, most of them in the family and Halloween-set rounds.

faqs.question: What's a hard Halloween movie trivia question?
faqs.answer: Ask what appears beside "The Monster" in the opening cast list of Frankenstein (1931). The answer is a question mark; the AFI Catalog notes that Boris Karloff's name appears only in the end credits.

faqs.question: How many questions should a Halloween movie quiz have?
faqs.answer: Thirty questions in three or four rounds is enough for one evening. By our untimed estimate that fills 35 to 45 minutes with marking, so keep the other rounds as spares.

faqs.question: Is Halloween movie trivia OK for kids?
faqs.answer: Yes, if you use the family and animated round and the films-set-on-Halloween round, which hold 5 of the 9 easy questions. Leave out the slasher round, because five of its six films are R-rated.

faqs.question: When did the original Halloween movie come out?
faqs.answer: John Carpenter's Halloween opened on 27 October 1978, according to its AFI Catalog record. It was also Jamie Lee Curtis's first feature film.

faqs.question: How do you score a movie trivia night fairly?
faqs.answer: Give 1 point per answer, accept surnames and ignore spelling, and give 2 points for an exact release year. Teams swap sheets to mark, and a closest-number tie-breaker settles draws.

faqs.question: How many people should be on a trivia team?
faqs.answer: Four to six suits a home party. A Swiss team pub quiz used groups of 5 to 7 and saw teamwork scores rise, and Sheffield medical students said they preferred competing as a team.

faqs.question: Was Nosferatu an official Dracula movie?
faqs.answer: No. Nosferatu (1922) is an unauthorized adaptation of Bram Stoker's Dracula, made in Germany by the studio Prana Film.

faqs.question: Can I run this quiz over a video call?
faqs.answer: Yes. Read each question aloud and have every team send its answers by private message at the end of each round, then reveal the answers before moving on.

faqs.question: Is the SubhSandesh Halloween card a quiz or party app?
faqs.answer: No. /happy-halloween is a greeting page for one person, with partner, bestie, family and kids modes, and it keeps no scores. Send it to the quiz winner instead: they carve a jack-o'-lantern, read your letter by flashlight and finish with a Boo License.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Halloween Movie Trivia: 53 Fact-Checked Questions and Answers

Here are 53 Halloween movie trivia questions with answers, in eight rounds from 1920s Universal monsters to Japanese, Korean and Indian horror, each tagged easy, medium or hard. Every answer was checked against the AFI Catalog or, for non-American films, Wikidata and Wikipedia, and anything unconfirmed was cut. If you send the answer key as a link, format it for small screens: across SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared-page views happen on phones, and the typical page is viewed 11.1 times (whole-site figures, none from Halloween).

## What counts as a fair movie trivia question?

A fair movie trivia question asks for one checkable fact, such as a name, a year or a place, with one answer a quizmaster can defend. It needs no clip, still or line of dialogue, so it works read aloud in a dark room.

Hard questions still earn their place. Across three preregistered experiments with 419 adults, [Liquin (2026, *Open Mind*)](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13056335) found that making a trivia answer costly to reach changed whether people chased it, but not how curious they felt.

## 53 Halloween movie trivia questions and answers, in 8 rounds

Each question carries a difficulty tag and a bold answer. Read each twice, then move on.

### 1. Classic monsters, 1920s to 1950s (8 questions)

Universal's monsters dominate here. The [AFI Catalog entry for *Frankenstein* (1931)](https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/moviedetails/3925) confirms questions 3, 34 and 53.

1. **Easy.** Universal's *Dracula* (1931) was based on an 1897 novel by which author? **Bram Stoker.**
2. **Medium.** Which silent star, cast first as Dracula, died in 1930 before filming? **Lon Chaney.**
3. **Hard.** In the opening credits of *Frankenstein* (1931), what appears beside "The Monster" instead of an actor's name? **A question mark.**
4. **Medium.** Who directed *Frankenstein* (1931), *The Invisible Man* (1933) and *Bride of Frankenstein* (1935)? **James Whale.**
5. **Hard.** *The Phantom of the Opera* (1925) adapts a 1910 novel by which French writer? **Gaston Leroux.**
6. **Medium.** *The Invisible Man* (1933) adapts a novel by which author? **H. G. Wells.**
7. **Medium.** *Creature from the Black Lagoon* (1954) was shot in which format that needed special glasses? **3-D.**
8. **Hard.** Per *Variety*, *The Wolf Man* (1941) was the first film in which its star dropped which suffix? **"Jr." (Lon Chaney Jr.).**

### 2. Slashers (8 questions)

These ask about credits and settings, not gore. Five of the six films are R-rated, so keep it for teenagers and adults.

9. **Easy.** Which director made both *A Nightmare on Elm Street* (1984) and *Scream* (1996)? **Wes Craven.**
10. **Medium.** *A Nightmare on Elm Street* was the feature debut of which later star, cast as Glen? **Johnny Depp.**
11. **Easy.** Who made her feature debut as Laurie Strode in *Halloween* (1978)? **Jamie Lee Curtis.**
12. **Hard.** Which friend of John Carpenter is credited as "The Shape", the masked killer, in *Halloween*? **Nick Castle.**
13. **Medium.** In which year are the opening murders of *Friday the 13th* (1980) set? **1958.**
14. **Medium.** *Psycho* (1960) adapts a 1959 novel by which writer? **Robert Bloch.**
15. **Hard.** What early working title did *The Texas Chain Saw Massacre* (1974) carry? **Leatherface.**
16. **Medium.** Who wrote *Scream* (1996)? **Kevin Williamson.**

### 3. Family and animated (8 questions)

Give this round to the youngest team. Five of its six films are rated PG in the US; *The Addams Family* is PG-13.

17. **Easy.** What is Jack Skellington's ghost dog called in *The Nightmare Before Christmas* (1993)? **Zero.**
18. **Hard.** Danny Elfman sings Jack's songs. Who provides Jack's speaking voice? **Chris Sarandon.**
19. **Medium.** Which Portland, Oregon, studio made the stop-motion film *Coraline* (2009)? **Laika.**
20. **Medium.** *Coraline* adapts a book by which author? **Neil Gaiman.**
21. **Easy.** What is the talking cat called in *Hocus Pocus* (1993)? **Binx (Thackery Binx).**
22. **Medium.** The title ghost of *Beetlejuice* (1988) is named after a star in which constellation? **Orion.**
23. **Easy.** In *Ghostbusters* (1984), which marshmallow mascot does Ray accidentally summon? **The Stay Puft Marshmallow Man.**
24. **Hard.** In *The Addams Family* (1991), whose hand plays Thing? **Magician-actor Christopher Hart's.**

### 4. Films set on Halloween (6 questions)

Every story here unfolds on 31 October, so it makes a natural opener. The [AFI Catalog entry for *Halloween* (1978)](https://catalog.afi.com/Catalog/moviedetails/56347) confirms questions 11, 12 and 26.

25. **Easy.** How does Elliott sneak E.T. outdoors on Halloween in *E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial* (1982)? **Under a sheet, as his costumed sister.**
26. **Easy.** *Halloween* (1978) opens on Halloween night 1963. How old is Michael Myers? **Six.**
27. **Medium.** On which day does Mortimer Brewster marry in *Arsenic and Old Lace* (1944)? **Halloween.**
28. **Medium.** Name the three actresses who play the Sanderson sisters in *Hocus Pocus*. **Bette Midler, Sarah Jessica Parker and Kathy Najimy (a point each).**
29. **Medium.** Which 1982 sequel drops Michael Myers for a plot about Silver Shamrock Novelties masks? ***Halloween III: Season of the Witch*.**
30. **Hard.** Who directed *Halloween III: Season of the Witch*? **Tommy Lee Wallace.**

### 5. Behind the scenes (8 questions)

This round rewards readers of film history. All eight answers come from production or Oscar records, not plot.

31. **Medium.** What did Alfred Hitchcock say he used for the blood in *Psycho*? **Chocolate syrup.**
32. **Hard.** What did William Castle call the skeleton that flew over audiences at *House on Haunted Hill* (1958)? **Emergo.**
33. **Medium.** *Night of the Living Dead* (1968) was filmed near which Pennsylvania city? **Pittsburgh.**
34. **Hard.** How do the screen credits of *Frankenstein* (1931) name novelist Mary Shelley? **"Mrs. Percy B. Shelley".**
35. **Hard.** *The Exorcist* (1973) was the first horror film nominated in which Oscar category? **Best Picture.**
36. **Medium.** Which writer won Best Adapted Screenplay for *The Exorcist*, adapting his own novel? **William Peter Blatty.**
37. **Medium.** *Young Frankenstein* (1974) reused lab gear Kenneth Strickfaden built for which film? ***Frankenstein* (1931).**
38. **Medium.** *The Silence of the Lambs* (1991) won Best Picture plus which two acting Oscars? **Best Actor (Anthony Hopkins) and Best Actress (Jodie Foster).**

### 6. International horror (8 questions)

The AFI Catalog covers American films, so these answers were checked against Wikidata and Wikipedia. Two are Indian.

39. **Easy.** *The Ring* (2002) remade a 1998 film from which country? **Japan (*Ring*, or *Ringu*).**
40. **Hard.** Who directed *Ring* (1998)? **Hideo Nakata.**
41. **Medium.** Which studio produced *Godzilla* (1954)? **Toho.**
42. **Medium.** *Nosferatu* (1922) is an unauthorized adaptation of which novel? ***Dracula*.**
43. **Medium.** Who directed the South Korean monster film *The Host* (2006)? **Bong Joon-ho.**
44. **Hard.** *Kwaidan* (1964) adapts ghost stories collected by which writer? **Lafcadio Hearn.**
45. **Hard.** Hindi horror-comedy *Bhool Bhulaiyaa* (2007) remakes which 1993 Malayalam film? ***Manichitrathazhu*.**
46. **Medium.** *Tumbbad* (2018) is set in a village in which Indian state? **Maharashtra.**

### 7. Name the year, no pictures (6 questions)

Read each title aloud; teams write its release year. An exact year scores 2, and within two years scores 1.

47. *Dracula*, the Bela Lugosi version: **1931.**
48. *Psycho*: **1960.**
49. *Night of the Living Dead*: **1968.**
50. *Halloween*, John Carpenter's original: **1978.**
51. *Ghostbusters*: **1984.**
52. *Get Out*: **2017.**

### 8. Tie-breaker (1 question)

Closest number wins. Nobody may change a written answer.

53. Per the AFI Catalog, what did *Frankenstein* (1931) finally cost? **$291,129.**

## The 8 rounds compared: questions, difficulty and best crowd

The table pairs rounds by audience, counting the difficulty tags above. Any two of the first three rows make a 30-question night.

| Rounds | Questions | Easy / medium / hard | Best for |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 Classic monsters + 7 Name the year | 14 | 1 / 4 / 3, plus 6 years | Adults and grandparents |
| 2 Slashers + 5 Behind the scenes | 16 | 2 / 9 / 5 | Horror fans aged 15+ |
| 3 Family and animated + 4 Set on Halloween | 14 | 5 / 6 / 3 | Mixed ages, 8 and up |
| 6 International + 8 Tie-breaker | 9 | 1 / 4 / 3, plus tie-breaker | Film buffs |

Rounds 3 and 4 hold 5 of the 9 easy questions. Lead with them when children play.

## How to host a Halloween movie trivia night: teams of 4 to 6, about 40 minutes

Play in teams. In a Swiss study, 197 healthcare students in groups of 5 to 7 took a 90-minute team pub quiz, and their teamwork scores rose ([Büsser et al., *BMC Medical Education*, 2025](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC12492745)). At Sheffield, 85 medical students preferred competing as a team over competing alone ([Finch, *The Clinical Teacher*, 2026](https://europepmc.org/article/PMC/PMC13101406)).

These rules suit 10 to 25 guests. Our untimed estimate: 30 questions fill 35 to 45 minutes, marking included.

- **Teams:** 4 to 6 players; at a family party, mix ages within each team.
- **Timing:** read each question twice, then allow 30 seconds.
- **Scoring:** 1 point per answer, 2 for an exact year. Surnames count; spelling doesn't.
- **Phones:** face down. A peek forfeits the round.
- **Answers:** reveal them after each round.

Give each team one answer sheet per round, in an identical layout. Teams swap sheets for marking, so nobody grades their own.

- Team name and round number at the top.
- Numbered lines 1 to 8.
- A round-total box for the marker.
- The tie-breaker on a separate strip.

For mixed ages, let under-12s answer easy questions alone for double points. That stops adults answering over them.

## After the quiz: one interactive Halloween card for the champion

Our [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) can't host a quiz; it is built for a single recipient, with English text and four modes (partner, bestie, family, kids). Make one for the champion: they pick trick or treat, clear misty portraits to reveal your pictures, then mix a potion out of memories you supplied. Site-wide, 90.9% of pages begun end up published and shared.

The [cinematic premium page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) holds a voice clip capped at 60 seconds plus 12 photos. Use it to deliver the quizmaster's verdict aloud.

## When a movie quiz is the wrong game: 3 cases

Trivia rewards people who have seen the films. With guests under about 8, adults answer while children wait, so pick an active game.

It also stalls when one team knows everything by round 2; make that film buff the quizmaster. And if you need a live scoreboard, our card isn't one.

auditReport.honestAssessment: An answer engine has a reason to lift this page because each of its 53 answers traces to a named film record (AFI Catalog, or Wikidata and Wikipedia for non-American films), with difficulty tags and a mixed-age hosting plan, while the measured top 10 holds one 200-question Jotform list (no outbound sources, no per-question difficulty tags, checked 2026-10-13), a 10-question DivX comedy quiz and seven hijacked-subdomain spam pages. The first-party numbers (48.3% phone views, 11.1 views per page, 90.9% publish rate) are platform-wide and only loosely tied to a quiz, and jotform.com's domain authority is far above ours, so the page can match it on accuracy but not on authority or volume.

structuralLimitations: SERP: one WebSearch (US index, 2026-10-13). Top 9: jotform.com 200 horror trivia questions (fetched), divx.com 10-question comedy quiz (fetched), and 7 hijacked-subdomain spam results (support-3.tychesoftwares.com x2, zkteco.tvc.mx x2, static.intrafocus.com x2, divx.com/?p=2374), counted weak; the tychesoftwares page timed out on fetch. Weak count 8 of 9.

Library of Congress (National Film Registry) and oscars.org returned 403 to automated fetches; per BRIEF §10 these were not worked around. American answers were verified on the AFI Catalog instead (30+ records fetched via its own search endpoint); international answers on Wikidata structured claims cross-checked with Wikipedia intros (verification only, not linked). BFI search returned 404.

Every answer was checked against the 211 Jotform questions: questions Jotform already asks (e.g. who plays Dracula 1931, Haddonfield, Hocus Pocus town, Train to Busan director, the Friday the 13th killer, Night of the Living Dead's working title) were replaced. Some film titles overlap, which is unavoidable.

Hosting section shares generic quiz conventions with Jotform's (teams, timed answers, a tie-breaker), which the task required; parameters differ (teams of 4 to 6 vs their 3 to 6; read twice and 30 s vs once and 20-30 s; 30 questions in 35-45 min).
Timing (35-45 minutes for 30 questions) is labelled in the body as our untimed estimate, not a measurement.

Dropped as unverifiable from non-competitor sources: the Michael Myers mask origin, Halloween's budget, Coco's Day of the Dead framing (AFI record is credits-only), Get Out's Oscar (only Jotform and Wikidata), Tumbbad's language (Wikidata says Hindi; widely described as Marathi-rooted).
PLOS ONE (Whatley 2025, curiosity and age) was a strong mixed-age source but PLOS ONE already appears in 11 b3 posts, so it was not used.
No modern film dialogue is quoted; questions ask about credits, settings and production facts only.
